subject.title: Feature: trustedWebhooks for Discord — allow specific webhooks to trigger agent responses

question: Should Discord add a guild-scoped trusted webhook authority that bypasses the default bot-message drop, and may that authority map payloads onto a configured Discord user identity?
rationale: The requested behavior is narrower than `allowBots: true`, but it turns possession of a Discord webhook URL into authority to enter agent sessions, and `mapToUser` crosses sender authorization and session-identity boundaries.

options.title: Approve narrow webhook allowlist
options.body: Allow maintainers to design an explicit webhook-id allowlist that can pass the bot-message gate, while keeping user impersonation/mapping disallowed or separately constrained until its authorization semantics are defined.

options.title: Approve mapped user authority
options.body: Permit `mapToUser` only with strict validation against configured guild users, clear audit/logging behavior, and tests proving it cannot bypass sender authorization or session isolation.

options.title: Decline Discord-native webhook ingress
options.body: Keep Discord bot-message policy unchanged and direct external automation to the authenticated Gateway/Webhooks plugin or a separate integration instead of adding another Discord config surface.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow webhook allowlist
recommendation.body: Allow maintainers to design an explicit webhook-id allowlist that can pass the bot-message gate, while keeping user impersonation/mapping disallowed or separately constrained until its authorization semantics are defined.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Discord preflight ownership and adjacent mention-policy work make this the best available routing candidate for the security/product decision.
